title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition - Guidance Q1 2026
author: Alex Chen
body:
Purpose
This document provides consolidated guidance for Redwood Inference finance and legal stakeholders on: budgeting & forecasting cadence and controls; standard contract lifecycle and legal intake process; procurement procedures and vendor onboarding; and revenue recognition and billing policies (RevRec). It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering managers responsible for budget ownership, vendor selection, contracting, and revenue reporting.

Scope
Applies to all spending, contracting, and revenue arrangements entered into by Redwood Inference effective FY2026 Q1 across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product lines and associated services (support, SLAs, professional services, observability add-ons).

Owners and RACI
- Document owner: Finance (Alex Chen)
- Legal owner: Contracts & Legal (Diego Ramirez)
- Procurement owner: Procurement lead (Priya Singh)
- Revenue recognition owner: Accounting (Maya Patel)

RACI (summary):
- Budget creation: Finance (R), Product/Engineering (A/C), Finance-legal (C)
- Contract review: Legal (R/A), Procurement (C), Requesting team (C)
- Vendor onboarding: Procurement (A), Security (C), Finance (C)
- RevRec determination: Accounting (R/A), Legal (C), Sales/Revenue ops (C)

1) Budgeting & Forecasting: Process and Controls
Overview:
- Annual planning: High-level revenue and expense targets set by executive leadership each November; Finance publishes target by business area by Dec 15.
- Quarterly reforecast: Rolling 12-month forecast updated at Q-end (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) with a detailed 3-month lookahead and a medium-term headcount & capacity plan.

Cadence and templates:
1. Budget kickoff (Nov 1): Finance issues templates (Google Sheets/Looker links) and target guidance.
2. Department submissions (Dec 10): Product/Eng/Go-to-market submit detailed budgets including headcount, cloud/GPU runoff, vendor commitments, R&D, and capital spend.
3. Executive review (Dec 20-31): Leadership reviews and finalizes.
4. Quarterly reforecast (days 10-15 after quarter close): Owners update actuals vs forecast, variance explanations, and actions.

Budget Controls and thresholds:
- Capital spend > $100k requires Finance + Legal + CEO approval.
- Non-recurring vendor contracts > $250k total contract value require CFO sign-off and Legal review.
- Headcount hires that inflate run-rate > $200k annually require People Ops + Finance approval.
- All recurring SaaS spend must be tagged to cost-centers and GL codes at purchase.

Required attachments for budget items > $50k:
- Business rationale (1 page)
- Expected ROI / payback timeline (months)
- Contract/PO draft if available
- Owner and timeline

2) Contracts & Legal Process
Standard lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: Requesting team opens contract intake in the CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management) system with template, required term highlights, and expected commercial team.
2. Triage & redlines: Legal reviews within 3 business days for standard contracts; proposer must highlight non-standard clauses.
3. Commercial negotiation: Procurement or Sales negotiates commercial terms; Legal approves final redlines.
4. Signature & storage: Contracts signed via DocuSign, stored in CLM and tagged with vendor, cost-center, and contract owner.

Key legal review focus areas:
- Data residency & customer data processing (align with security-and-compliance policies)
- IP ownership, model output licensing, and use limitations
- Liability caps, indemnity, and warranty clauses (standard cap is 3x fees or $1M minimum)
- SLA and uptime commitments (map to Redwood SLA tiers)
- Termination rights and transition assistance for Private deployments

SLAs and approvals matrix:
- Standard vendor agreement: Legal review within 3 days, Procurement approval within 5 days.
- Custom enterprise contract: Legal + Security + Finance review required; target review within 10 business days.
- Exceptions: Any clause that modifies liability, data residency, or indemnity must be escalated to Legal Director.

Contract metadata requirements (to be captured in CLM):
- Vendor legal name
- Contract start/end dates
- Renewal terms and auto-renewal notice period
- Total contract value (TCV) and annual recurring value (ARV)
- Owner (Team and Person)
- GL code and cost-center

3) Procurement Procedures and Vendor Onboarding
Vendor selection & evaluation:
- Standard RFP: For vendor spend > $100k TCV, procurement leads an RFP with at least 3 vendors where feasible.
- Evaluation criteria: Security posture, SLA, price per unit, integration effort, TCO (3-year), and references.
- Security & compliance: All vendors handling customer data must complete security questionnaire and sign Data Processing Addendum where required.

Purchase order / approval flow:
- Low-value (<= $10k): Direct purchase by cost-center owner with finance tagging.
- Medium-value ($10k < x <= $100k): Manager approval + Finance notification.
- High-value (> $100k): Procurement + Finance + Legal approvals and executive notification.

Vendor onboarding checklist (must be completed prior to first invoice payment):
- Execute contract and confirm signatory authority
- Add vendor to AP with W-9 / tax forms (or equivalent)
- Verify banking details via secure vendor portal or Finance team
- Assign GL codes and cost-center mapping
- Complete security questionnaire and DPA if applicable
- Establish initial payment terms (Net30 default; Net45/60 requires Finance approval)

Preferred payment terms and discounts:
- Standard: Net30 from invoice receipt, electronic payment (ACH).
- Early payment discounts: Consider if discount > 1% for Net10 and TCV impact positive.
- Capital vendor payment schedule: Escrow or milestone-based payment plans require Finance approval.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles (ASC 606 aligned):
- Identify contract(s) with customer: Signed agreement that creates enforceable rights and obligations.
- Identify performance obligations: Distinct goods/services (API calls, embeddings, Dedicated reserved capacity, private deployment professional services).
- Determine transaction price: Consider discounts, refunds, credits, and variable consideration (usage-based billing).
- Allocate transaction price to performance obligations.
- Recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied (over time or at a point in time).

Billing cadence and examples:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Bill monthly in arrears based on metered tokens/embeddings. Revenue recognized as usage occurs; estimate and adjust for variable consideration using expected value method when applicable.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Recognize monthly over the committed period for subscription fees. Upfront prepayments recognized as deferred revenue and amortized over the contract term.
- Private deployments & professional services: Recognize based on milestone completion or percentage-of-completion if criteria met and reliable estimates exist.

Common RevRec scenarios and treatment:
- Upfront implementation fee (non-refundable): If not distinct from subscription, allocate and recognize over term; if distinct and customer can benefit separately, recognize on completion.
- Free trial converting to paid: No revenue during free trial. On conversion, revenue recognized per standard rules.
- Usage credits / refunds: Treated as variable consideration; reserve vs. adjust invoices depending on timing and predictability.

Invoicing and collections:
- Invoice generation: Finance issues invoices monthly; usage invoices generated from billing system (Stripe/Zuora integration) and reconciled to usage reports.
- Payment terms: Standard Net30; enterprise customers may have custom terms documented in contract.
- Collections: Late invoices escalate to Sales/RPM and then to Finance collections team after 30 days. Collections process documented in AR playbook.

Revenue reporting and cutoffs:
- Month-end close: Finance reconciles billed revenue vs recognized revenue and updates deferred revenue schedules. Cutoffs follow calendar month boundaries; usage through 23:59 UTC of last day included in period.
- Quarterly close: RevRec analysis and climate check for material judgments (variable consideration, contract modifications).

Required documentation for RevRec audits:
- Executed contract and amendments
- Usage reports and billing extracts aligned to invoices
- Contracts mapping to performance obligations and allocation schedules
- Management sign-off on significant judgments (variable consideration > $50k or contract modifications)

Appendices
A. Approval matrix (summary):
- < $10k: Cost-center owner
- $10k - $100k: Manager + Finance notification
- $100k - $250k: Procurement + Finance + Legal review
- > $250k: CFO + Legal Director approval mandatory

B. Sample GL codes and tagging guidance:
- 6000: Cloud infrastructure (GPU)
- 6100: Third-party services (SaaS)
- 6200: Professional services (implementation)
- 7000: Revenue - Hosted API
- 7100: Revenue - Dedicated subscriptions
- 7200: Revenue - Professional services

C. Contract metadata checklist (CSV header example):
vendor_name,vendor_id,contract_id,start_date,end_date,tcv,arv,renewal_notice_days,owner,cost_center,gl_code,security_level

D. Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Who signs NDAs?
A: Standard partner NDAs can be signed by VP level (Legal delegated authority). Any NDA with data residency claims or unusual IP terms must be routed to Legal Director.

Q: How do I request an exception to payment terms?
A: Submit a payment-terms exception form to Finance with business rationale; Finance reviews with Treasury for cash implications.
